s5-hidden-gw.base: GW must behave as specified when driven only through its entry point GW_AppMain with software bus messages, its ConnTable, the shared CMDI.ValTable and traffic on its UDP, TCP and SERIAL connections, using only the names, structures, message IDs, function codes and event IDs defined in the specification.

cases.Startup and housekeeping: at start-up GW registers ConnTable (eight 152-byte GW_ConnDef_t, with a validation function), subscribes to its command, SEND_HK and WAKEUP message IDs, shares CMDI.ValTable, sends GW_INIT_INF_EID once, and answers SEND_HK with GW_HkTlm_t on GW_HK_TLM_MID in the specified field order; NOOP and SEND_CONN_STATUS count under CommandCounter
cases.Validation table share and retry: GW shares CMDI.ValTable with CFE_TBL_Share at initialization and, until it succeeds, again on every WAKEUP, sending one GW_VALTBL_ERR_EID per failure streak and GW_VALTBL_INF_EID on success; it calls CFE_TBL_GetAddress on the shared handle every WAKEUP, and when that fails (CMDI restarted) ValTableShared becomes 0 and GW shares the table again
cases.No traffic without the shared table: while ValTableShared is 0 GW reads nothing from its connections (inbound data waits) and egresses nothing, each skipped write counting as an egress error; once the table is shared again the waiting frames are processed
cases.Key change of the shared table: a table update of CMDI.ValTable takes effect for GW from its next WAKEUP: frames under the old key are rejected as HMAC, frames under the new key are accepted, and egress frames carry a MAC under the new key
cases.Connection definition validation: ADD_CONN rejects with GW_CONN_ADD_ERR_EID and a command error, leaving the slot unused: Index 8 or above, a used slot, Interface outside 1..3, Enabled other than 0 or 1, for UDP and TCP an unterminated or non-dotted-IPv4 RemoteAddr or RemotePort 0, for TCP and SERIAL a nonzero LocalPort, for SERIAL an unterminated DevicePath or one not starting with /, duplicate used MIDs in Subs, and two UDP connections sharing a nonzero LocalPort; valid definitions are accepted with GW_CONN_ADD_INF_EID
cases.Connection table validation: the ConnTable validation function applies the definition rules of S5.1 to every used slot, including LocalPort uniqueness across UDP slots, and reports a rejected table with GW_TBL_VAL_ERR_EID
cases.Egress framing: each subscribed packet is written to every enabled connection listing its MID as one CMDI frame built with CMDVAL_HmacSha256 and CMDVAL_Crc16 under the shared table's key: Version 1, Flags 0, SourceId the node ID, TimeSeconds the onboard seconds, Sequence a per-connection counter from 1, the packet unchanged; PacketsEgressed and TxPackets count each write
cases.Egress source is the node ID: egress frames carry GW's node ID (CFE_PSP_GetProcessorId) as SourceId
cases.Egress errors: a packet longer than 1024 bytes is not framed and counts as an egress error; GW_EGRESS_ERR_EID is sent once per connection until its next successful write while EgressErrors always increments; a failed UDP write disables the connection with GW_CONN_DOWN_ERR_EID
cases.Subscription bookkeeping: GW subscribes with a message limit of 16 to the union of the enabled connections' Subs, unsubscribes MIDs no longer needed whenever the union changes (DISABLE, ENABLE, REMOVE), and reports the union's size as Subscriptions
cases.UDP ingress and rejection reasons: every inbound datagram is one frame (FramesReceived) validated with CMDVAL_ValidateFrame against the shared table and GW's onboard seconds; an accepted frame's command is published unchanged (PacketsIngressed, RxPackets); a rejection counts under FormatErrors, CrcErrors, HmacErrors, SourceErrors or AgeErrors and the connection's RxErrors, publishes nothing, and sends one GW_FRAME_REJECT_ERR_EID naming the connection index, the reason and, except for FORMAT, the source ID; a datagram whose size is not 50 + L is FORMAT
cases.Ingress batch per wakeup: every WAKEUP GW reads without blocking up to 16 frames per enabled connection, leaving the rest for the next WAKEUP
cases.Loop rule: an accepted embedded command whose MID is in the Subs of any enabled connection is dropped and counted under LoopDrops, not published
cases.TCP connection and stream framing: a TCP connection is CONNECTING while no listener exists and GW retries once per second; it reaches UP with GW_CONN_UP_INF_EID when the listener appears; writes skipped while CONNECTING count as egress errors; on TCP each frame is preceded by the marker 1A CF FC 1D both ways, partial frames are kept across wakeups, bytes before a marker are skipped, a header whose L is outside 8..1024 is a FORMAT rejection after which hunting resumes, and a peer close returns the connection to CONNECTING
cases.TCP read failure: a read failure on a connection is an ingress error (IngressErrors, GW_INGRESS_ERR_EID) and returns a TCP connection to CONNECTING, from which it reconnects
cases.Serial connection and stream framing: a SERIAL connection opens its DevicePath (a PTY slave) and carries marker-framed CMDI frames both ways, including frames split across writes, garbage before a marker and a frame with a bad MAC
cases.Serial reads never block: reads of a PTY never block GW's main loop: with nothing pending a read returns at once, GW keeps answering housekeeping requests and sends its heartbeat once per second
cases.Restart with an existing serial mapping: after ES STOP_APP and START_APP, with the /dev/pts mapping and other OSAL resources left by the stopped instance, GW initializes without failing and carries traffic over a new SERIAL connection
cases.Connection commands: DISABLE_CONN, ENABLE_CONN (opening at once; an open failure rejects it), REMOVE_CONN and RELOAD (re-applying the active table and discarding command changes) behave as specified with their INF events, and invalid uses are rejected with their ERR events and counted as command errors
cases.Connection table update: a ConnTable update is applied like RELOAD: connections are closed, the table's definitions are opened and connections added by command are discarded
cases.Open failures: an enabled ADD_CONN whose open or bind fails (UDP bind, SERIAL device) is rejected with GW_CONN_ADD_ERR_EID, leaving the slot unused
cases.Connection status and housekeeping: SEND_CONN_STATUS reports per slot Interface, Enabled, State (DISABLED 0, UP 1, CONNECTING 2), SubCount and the counters, and housekeeping reports ConnectionsConfigured, ConnectionsUp, Subscriptions and ValTableShared
cases.Reset counters: RESET_COUNTERS zeroes the command counters, PacketsEgressed, PacketsIngressed, EgressErrors, IngressErrors, LoopDrops, FramesReceived, the five reason counters and the per-connection counters, but not ConnectionsConfigured, ConnectionsUp, Subscriptions or ValTableShared
cases.Command errors: an unknown function code gives GW_CC_ERR_EID, a wrong command length GW_CMD_LEN_ERR_EID and an unexpected message ID GW_MID_ERR_EID, each counted as a command error
cases.Heartbeat: GW sends SFI_HeartbeatCmd_t on SFI_HEARTBEAT_MID every 10th WAKEUP, naming GW, with Sequence 1 for the first heartbeat and +1 per heartbeat
